Any earlier, context-specific references (including those in the Sale Law of 1968) presupposed rather than originated this overarching duty, functioning merely as applications once the general principle had been codified. 7.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: The split between Agency Law and Contracts (General Part) Law highlights a key distinction the question requires us to resolve. By contrast, the Contracts (General Part) Law placed an explicit, trans-substantive duty of good faith at the very foundation of the emerging civil code, declaring it applicable to the negotiation, formation, and performance of all contractual relations. Subsequent statutes simply drew upon this general principle rather than originating it. Treating a narrow sectoral clause as the conceptual starting point would overlook how Israeli jurisprudence itself came to view the 1973 codification as the decisive moment when good faith entered the system as a unifying norm.
